method: An ISO 8601 duration is a P followed by years, months, weeks and days, then a T before hours, minutes and seconds, so P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S is one year, two months, three days, four hours, five minutes and six seconds. The parser accepts each unit at most once and only in that order, allows a decimal fraction only in the smallest unit present, refuses fractions on years and months because a month has no fixed length, and refuses a week designator mixed with other units, as ISO 8601 requires. Calendar months are added the way a calendar does it: the month is advanced and the day is clamped to the target month's last day, so 31 January plus one month is 28 February, or 29 February in a leap year, and 29 February plus one year is 28 February. Weeks and days are then added as fixed 24-hour periods, and the time of day is added last against the start time, rounded to the nearest second with halves rounded up. All date arithmetic runs on UTC so a daylight-saving change cannot shift the result. Totals are exact when the duration has no years or months; when it does, they are nominal and use 1 month = 30 days, which is stated in the labels rather than presented as an exact figure. Results are shown to three decimal places with trailing zeros removed. Everything runs in the browser, so nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
